messages:
arya: Quick sync — need to pick the next batch of models to onboard for the Q2 sprint. Customers (Atlas, FinOps) are pushing for faster responses and better long-form summarization. Proposing we use a RICE-ish scoring + a sequencing heuristic (latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive). Thoughts?

mike: +1 on RICE. Also we should factor in quantization maturity per model — engineering effort isn't just parameter count.

sophia: Agree. For summarization we saw big metric jumps with Llama3-70B over 33B in our evals, but cost/latency was worse. Could be a candidate if we pair with 4-bit quantization and CPU offload.

caleb: Customer asks: Atlas explicitly asked for sub-300ms median for short prompts. That rules out some large variants unless we can route small requests to a cheaper variant.

jen: Sales perspective: if we can promise better long-form quality for Finance customers, they'll convert to Dedicated more often. Impact is high even if reach is initially small. :moneybag:

mike: Proposal sketch (quick RICE table):
```
Model Variant         Reach   Impact  Confidence  Effort  RICE_score
Llama3-70B q4         2      8       0.7         6       18.7
Mistral-7B v2         5      5       0.9         2       56.25
Llama2-13B chat       7      4       0.95        1       266.5
Embedder-Mistral 3B   9      6       0.8         2       216
```
(rough numbers — just to surface tradeoffs)

sophia: That table mixes different goal types (chat, embeddings, summarization). We should compute RICE per goal and then sequence by cross-goal constraints (latency, infra readiness).

arya: Good point. Let's break into two lanes: 1) latency-first (short prompt/chat/interactive) and 2) quality-first (long-form summarization/batched jobs). Sequence onboarding so each lane has at least one high-impact variant in the sprint.

caleb: Operational constraints: dedicated infra for 70B q4 is limited. Also need canary policy: 2% traffic, rollback window 24h, success criteria: latency P50 < 400ms for interactive and qualitative evals show >=5% improvement on our summarization suite.

mike: Implementation plan suggestion:
- Sprint week 1: infra prep + quant toolchain for 4-bit q4
- Week 2: model build + local perf runs
- Week 3: private canary (internal teams) + evals
- Week 4: public canary 2% then ramp if metrics hold
(estimate: ~3.5 engineer-weeks + 0.5 infra ops)

jen: Can we gate the public canary on a sales signal? If Atlas signs letter of intent we can prioritize ramp. Otherwise hold.

arya: I like gating on a lightweight LOI. But don't let LOI be the only trigger — we should also decide by confidence on quantized perf. If confidence >= 0.8 and infra cost fits, we go.

sophia: For embeddings lane, Mistral small looks cheap and high reach. We can onboard that in parallel with a small team (embedding infra is simpler). Recommend parallelize embedding onboarding with 1 engineer.

caleb: Proposed acceptance criteria (concise):
- Latency lane: P50 < 400ms, P95 < 900ms, error rate < 0.5% under 2% canary for 24h
- Quality lane: eval BLEU/ROUGE/QA >= baseline + 5% on our summarization set and no regression on hallucination checks
- Embeddings: cosine sim > baseline + 3% on customer eval set, inference cost < target

mike: One more risk: kernel selection for q4 on our runtime can regress generation quality for some models. Need a holdout eval for safety-critical prompts (Finance).

arya: Decision proposal (we should vote quickly):
1) Prioritize onboarding Mistral-7B v2 for embeddings (parallel) — high reach, low effort.
2) Sequence Llama3-70B q4 for quality lane but gate public canary on LOI or confidence >=0.8.
3) Keep Llama2-13B chat as fallback low-effort variant for interactive routing.

caleb: :thumbsup: from ops. Will draft canary doc and rollout policy.

jen: +1 from sales, will try to surface LOI from Atlas this week.

mike: I'll spike kernel/quant experiments Monday.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: new canary policy template created by @caleb. See /deploys/canary-templates/llama3-70b-q4

arya: Thanks everyone. I'll write up the brief with RICE per lane and the acceptance criteria, then we can lock the sprint planning board. If anyone wants to adjust scores before I post, ping me by EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
